judgment.reasoning_summary: The polynomial P(x) is divisible by x^2 - 3x + 2 if and only if P(x) = (x^2 - 3x + 2)Q(x) for some polynomial Q(x). Since x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2), we need P(x) to be divisible by both (x - 1) and (x - 2). By the Remainder Theorem, P(1) = 0 and P(2) = 0. We can solve these equations to find the smallest positive integer n.
